results.title: Netflix to launch new 'Class Wars' series with focus on music
results.content: Netflix will launch the competition show "Vocal Class Wars" next year, following the success of its megahit series "Culinary Class Wars," the streaming platform said Wednesday. Following the format of the cooking competition show, the upcoming series pits anonymous singers against musicians that have already become household names, according to Netflix. It will be directed by Kim Hak-min, the producer behind "Culinary Class Wars," and Park Sung-hwan, known for producing "Just Makeup." The duo previously collaborated on the music audition show "Sing Again." "Culinary Class Wars" is one of Netflix's hit original Korean shows, with the third season in the making. The show's first season topped Netflix's chart for most-popular non-English TV shows for three consecutive weeks.

results.title: Seoul rolls out 6 night coupon packs to keep tourists exploring after dark
results.content: Seoul is looking to turn its nights into a bigger draw for international visitors, introducing six themed discount packages designed to encourage tourists to stay out longer and spend more across the city. The Seoul Tourism Organization announced Wednesday that it is expanding nighttime attractions available through its Discover Seoul Pass and launching six Night Coupon Packs covering dining, shopping, wellness, sightseeing and cultural experiences. The initiative follows growing demand for after-dark activities among foreign visitors. According to the organization's analysis of pass usage, nighttime visits between 6 p.m. and 6 a.m. accounted for 14 percent of partner-facility visits in 2024 and 15.2 percent in both 2025 and 2026, as of Nov. 1. results.title: EXO's Kai, Sehun to debut as duo EXO-KASE on Dec. 1
results.content: Kai and Sehun of K-pop boy band EXO will debut as a new duo, EXO-KASE, on Dec. 1 with their first EP, “Waking Up The City,” their agency SM Entertainment said Wednesday. Fans have long paired the two, both born in 1994, under the nickname “94-liners,” a reference to the Korean fan practice of grouping idols by birth year. The agency billed the act as a “visual performance unit” that pairs Kai’s intense, “hot guy” charisma with Sehun’s chic, “cool guy” image. In K-pop, a unit, or subunit, is a smaller group formed by members of an existing band to release music with a concept separate from the full group. EXO debuted in 2012 and has previously released music through units such as EXO-CBX and EXO-SC, the latter of which included Sehun. The EP contains seven tracks in a range of moods, including the title track and a solo song by each member, according to the agency. “More than anything, th

results.title: Korea climbs 8 spots to rank 10th in global digital, AI competitiveness
results.content: Korea jumped eight places to rank 10th out of 70 nations in the 2026 World Digital and AI Competitiveness Ranking (WDAIR), published Wednesday by the International Institute for Management Development (IMD) — the prestigious Swiss business school known for its benchmark global competitiveness evaluations. Among nations with populations exceeding 20 million, Korea secured fourth place, trailing only the United States, Canada and China. The Ministry of Science and ICT announced that Korea achieved comprehensive improvements across all five evaluated categories: Governance, Technological Infrastructure, Efficiency, Human Resources Development and Societal Attitudes & Values. Notably, Korea jumped 10 places to rank third globally in Efficiency and climbed four spots to third in Technological Infrastructure. results.title: Sangmidang expands food bank support with 2 refrigerated trucks
results.content: Sangmidang Holdings said Wednesday that its charitable foundation donated two refrigerated trucks to the Korea Foodbank on Tuesday, expanding a delivery support program launched to help local food banks safely transport donated food. The latest contribution brings the total number of trucks provided since the foundation signed a partnership agreement in October 2022 to 12. The foundation plans to provide eight more by 2030. Sangmidang Holdings Chairman Hur Young-in and Kim Hyun-hoon, president of the Korea National Council on Social Welfare, attended the handover ceremony in Dongjak District in Seoul. The company also donated 4,000 bakery products, which were loaded onto the trucks. The vehicles will serve Busanjin District in Busan and Gyeryong, South Chungcheong Province. results.title: AMCHAM raises $127,000 for student scholarships
results.content: The American Chamber of Commerce in Korea (AMCHAM) raised a record 175 million won ($127,000) for university scholarships at its annual charity event on Tuesday, bringing together business leaders to support students from financially disadvantaged backgrounds. The total marked a 17 percent increase from the 150 million won raised a year earlier. Organized by AMCHAM’s Partners for the Future Foundation, the event featured 44 CEOs and senior executives from member companies volunteering as servers, personally serving dinner to approximately 440 guests. The number of executive volunteers increased from 41 last year. Now in its 19th year, CEO Servers’ Night is one of AMCHAM’s signature charity events, bringing business leaders out of their boardrooms to serve guests and raise funds for university students in financial need. “CEO Servers’ Night brings business leaders together in a different

results.title: Yoon Ga-eun's 'The World of Love' expands global release to UK, Japan, North America
results.content: Director Yoon Ga-eun’s “The World of Love” is preparing for another wave of international releases, with theatrical debuts in Britain, Japan and North America scheduled for the second half of 2026, extending the film’s growing presence across Asia and Europe. The film, which opened in Korea on Oct. 22, 2025, has already reached audiences in Hong Kong, Singapore, Taiwan and France, where its sustained theatrical runs have drawn attention to its international appeal. In Hong Kong, the film played for 15 weeks after opening Jan. 29, while its French release on May 6 resulted in an 11-week run, according to distributor Barunson E&A. The film follows Ju-in, an 18-year-old high school student whose refusal to join a schoolwide petition campaign triggers a series of mysterious notes, setting off a story about social pressure and the complexities of adolescence. results.title: Theborn Korea enlists Italy's UNOX for K-food rollout
results.content: Global food service and restaurant franchise operator, Theborn Korea, has partnered with Italian oven manufacturer UNOX to program its standardized recipes into commercial equipment, paving the way for an automated K-food rollout across Europe. Theborn Korea said Wednesday it signed a memorandum of understanding with UNOX on Nov. 4 at the Italian company's headquarters, combining its expertise in Korean cuisine and TBK sauces with UNOX's commercial cooking technology. Under the agreement, the companies will test Korean dishes using 11 varieties of TBK sauces and convert cooking conditions into data to develop standardized recipes and operating manuals. The goal is to allow local restaurant workers with little experience preparing Korean food to produce dishes with consistent taste and quality using UNOX smart ovens. results.title: Bus rams into 32 vehicles in Bundang, 48 injured
results.content: SEONGNAM — A bus plowed into more than 30 vehicles waiting at a traffic stop in Seongnam, just south of Seoul, during morning rush hour, officials said, leaving 48 people injured. The city bus, driven by a man in his 60s, collided with four other buses, a cargo truck and 27 passenger cars before coming to a stop after hitting a traffic barrier in Seongnam's Bundang Ward at 7:34 a.m. The collision left 48 people hurt, including six with serious injuries. None of the injuries were reported to be life threatening. The 60-something bus driver was not found to be under the influence of alcohol. The driver reportedly told police that the brakes did not work, with investigators looking into the exact cause of the crash.

results.title: Revised regional currency swap arrangement takes effect
results.content: A revision of the Chiang Mai Initiative Multilateralisation (CMIM), a multilateral currency swap arrangement among Korea, China, Japan and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), took effect Wednesday, the Bank of Korea said. All 13 members of the ASEAN+3 group have completed their internal procedures for signing the revised agreement, which was endorsed at the ASEAN+3 Finance Ministers' and Central Bank Governors' Meeting in May 2025, according to the BOK. The revised CMIM includes the Rapid Financing Facility, which provides prompt financial assistance to members facing urgent balance of payments needs. It took effect Wednesday, seven days after the completion of the signing procedures, the central bank said. Launched in 2010, the CMIM is a multilateral currency swap arrangement among ASEAN+3 members aimed at providing liquidity to member economies in times of financial cri

results.title: Gwanghwamun Square to glow blue in tribute to 23 UN Korean War allies
results.content: Gwanghwamun Square in downtown Seoul will glow blue Wednesday evening, as Seoul invites residents and visitors to honor United Nations veterans whose sacrifices helped defend Korea's freedom and peace during the 1950-53 Korean War. The Seoul Metropolitan Government will hold a public memorial at the Garden of Gratitude on Wednesday, marking UN Veterans International Memorial Day with candlelight, a special lighting ceremony and opportunities for citizens to share messages of appreciation. The evening program will begin after sunset with a candle-lighting event, allowing visitors to receive free LED candles and gather around the installation known as Lights of Gratitude 23. At 8 p.m., 23 lights representing countries that sent troops to the Korean War will glow blue, the color associated with the United Nations. results.title: Turbulent geopolitics: 'Korean Dream' initiative can be a path forward
results.content: As the Sinamrok River Bridge — a core logistical gateway on the North Korea–China border — officially opens and North Korean leader Kim Jong-un makes a visit to Dandong, China, the Northeast Asian geopolitical landscape is rapidly restructuring into a tightly knit North Korea–China–Russia axis. Having gained nuclear capabilities, North Korea has secured external and economic safeguards through China and Russia, emboldening Kim Jong-un to aggressively push his “hostile two-state doctrine” and sever all ties with South Korea. This tectonic shift not only renders South Korea’s traditional appeasement policies obsolete but also diminishes any realistic expectations for meaningful breakthroughs in potential future U.S.–North Korea summits. results.title: Gov't to release growth forecasts 3 times per year: finance minister
results.content: Korea's top economic policymaker said Wednesday the government will release annual economic growth forecasts three times a year starting in 2027, up from the current two, to respond more proactively to changing economic conditions. Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il made the announcement as he discussed details of the government's economic growth strategy for next year with relevant ministers, indicating the plan will seek sustainable growth by addressing disparities. "In order to promptly respond to the changing environment at home and abroad, the government will increase the number of economic outlooks issued from two to three, which would mark the first change in 32 years," Lee said. results.title: Korea ranks 10th place in global AI, digital competitiveness
results.content: Korea came in 10th place among 70 countries in a global digital and artificial intelligence (AI) competitiveness ranking, the science ministry said Wednesday. The country moved up eight spots from the previous year, according to the report published by the International Institute for Management Development, a Swiss-based business school, according to the ministry. Taking the top spot this year was the United States, rising from its fourth spot a year ago. Canada, however, lost its top-spot position to be ranked at fifth place this year. Among countries in the Asia-Pacific region, Singapore was ranked second place, China came in at seventh place, and Japan ranked 19th place. By category, Korea ranked third in the technology infrastructure and efficiency metrics. results.title: Exports more than double in 1st 10 days of November
results.content: Korea's exports more than doubled in the first 10 days of November from a year earlier, customs data showed Wednesday, bringing the country closer to reaching $1 trillion in annual exports. Outbound shipments reached $33.5 billion in the Nov. 1-10 period, compared with $15.7 billion a year earlier, according to data from the Korea Customs Service. It was the highest export value recorded for the first 10 days of any November. Imports rose 45 percent on-year to $24.7 billion over the cited period, resulting in a trade surplus of $8.8 billion. By sector, exports of chips soared 331.2 percent to $16.6 billion. Semiconductors accounted for 49.7 percent of the total outbound shipments, up 25.3 percentage points from a year earlier. Outbound shipments of petroleum products also more than doubled to $2 billion over the period. Exports of cars, on the other hand, fell 4.3 percent to $1.4 billion

results.title: Korea to extend fuel tax cuts through January to ease price burdens
results.content: Korea will extend its fuel tax cuts by another two months through January to ease the financial burden on the public amid lingering uncertainty in the Middle East, the finance ministry said Wednesday. The Ministry of Finance and Economy said the decision was made at a meeting of economy-related ministers chaired by Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il, taking into account the need to ease the burden on households and the government's capacity to respond to future price volatility. Under the measure, the current tax cuts of 15 percent on gasoline and 25 percent on diesel and butane, originally set to expire at the end of this month, will remain in place through the end of January. The government has maintained the rates since May. results.title: Korea to launch task force to tackle disparities
results.content: Korea will launch a new task force led by the finance minister to address widening disparities across various sectors, the government said Wednesday. Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il unveiled the plan during a meeting with economy-related ministers, saying the task force will consist of five working groups tasked with addressing disparities in the labor market, industries, regions, generations and social classes. Each group will be led by a vice minister responsible for the respective area and work with state-run research institutes to identify key policy tasks. "The artificial intelligence transformation could deepen and accelerate disparities, leading to a K-shaped divide," the government said. results.title: Seoul shares up late Wednesday morning on tech rally amid rate hike worries
results.content: Seoul shares extended gains late Wednesday morning, led by a rebound in technology stocks, despite concerns that hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation could prompt further interest rate hikes. After opening 0.56 percent lower, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) reversed course and was trading up 35.68 points, or 0.68 percent, at 5,274.81 as of 11:20 a.m. On Tuesday, the index gained 4.39 percent, buoyed by a rally in U.S. technology stocks and falling oil prices. Overnight, the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 0.3 percent, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq composite declined 0.74 percent. U.S. consumer prices rose 0.3 percent in October from the previous month, exceeding market expectations and fueling concerns that the Federal Reserve could pursue a more aggressive monetary tightening policy to curb inflation. results.title: 'Dead-End Job' tops Netflix's non-English TV chart
results.content: The Korean original series "Dead-End Job" has topped Netflix's non-English TV series chart, the streaming platform said Wednesday. The Netflix series, released Oct. 30, accumulated 8.7 million views during the latest tracking week ending Sunday, according to Netflix. The series, starring Lee Jae-wook and Kim Min-ha, blends horror and black comedy and satirizes South Korea's grind culture. It landed in the top 10 in 76 countries and topped the chart in 22 of them, including South Korea, Bolivia, Egypt, Indonesia and Vietnam. The Korean medical drama series "Doctor X: Mafia in White" ranked No. 4 with 3.7 million views. Based on the Japanese series "Doctor-X: Surgeon Michiko Daimon," it follows genius surgeon Gye Su-jeong (Kim Ji-won), who challenges corruption in her hospital. results.title: Fire breaks out again at shantytown in southern Seoul; no injuries reported
results.content: A fire broke out early Wednesday at a shantytown in Seoul's southern ward of Gangnam, but firefighters fully extinguished the blaze, officials said, with no injuries reported. The fire began at a home in Guryong Village at 4:28 a.m. before fire authorities put it out at 6:27 a.m. after mobilizing 105 personnel and 32 vehicles. Authorities plan to investigate the exact cause of the fire. The latest fire at the village came about two weeks following the Oct. 27 fire that forced 39 people to flee and left one person with a minor injury. Many of the makeshift homes illegally built in the town are prone to fires as they are built with highly flammable materials.

results.title: S. Korean FM stresses bilateral trust following meeting with Ukraine counterpart
results.content: Foreign Minister Cho Hyun stressed mutual respect and trust as the foundation for bilateral relations during his talks with Ukrainian counterpart Andrii Sybiha, the Korean foreign ministry said Tuesday. It was their first meeting since a deepening rift emerged between the two countries over Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's September disclosure of the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war (POWs) to South Korea. Their discussion took place on the sidelines of the Group of Seven Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in France on Tuesday (local time). "Cho stressed that mutual respect, trust and the faithful implementation of agreements between countries are fundamental prerequisites for developing bilateral relations, expressing hope that all pending issues between the two countries will be resolved amicably," the ministry said in a press release. results.title: Korea adds 139,000 jobs in October, above 100,000 for 4th month
results.content: Korea added 139,000 jobs in October from a year earlier, government data showed Wednesday, with job growth exceeding the 100,000 mark for the fourth consecutive month. The number of employed people came to 29.17 million in October, compared with 29.04 million a year earlier, according to data from the Ministry of Data and Statistics. Job growth turned positive in June after declining by 40,000 in May, the first drop in 17 months. The country's jobless rate came to 2 percent last month, down 0.2 percentage point from a year earlier. The number of unemployed people totaled 602,000 in October, down 56,000 from the same month in 2025. The employment rate for people aged 15 to 64 came to 70.4 percent, up 0.3 percentage point from a year earlier. The figure for those aged 15 to 29, on the other hand, fell 1.7 percentage points to 42.9 percent.

results.content: WASHINGTON — Human Rights Watch (HRW) has urged the United Nations to address North Korea's human rights situation alongside security issues in future diplomatic engagement with Pyongyang. General Assembly should recommend that future dialogue with North Korea address human rights and security concerns together, rather than treating them as separate issues. General Assembly has the power to forge these connections, even as the Security Council remains deadlocked," Audrey Gregg, HRW's senior coordinator for Asia, wrote in a commentary published Monday. results.title: Taiwan, China tap market rescue funds. Why won't Korea?
results.content: China and Taiwan have tapped market rescue funds to reverse last week's sharp stock sell-off, triggered by the U.S. midterm elections. Korea, meanwhile, is holding back, resisting calls from retail investors to deploy what policymakers consider a weapon of last resort. KOSPI has shed 11.13 percent since the start of November as of Monday, leaving the benchmark down 42.87 percent from its June 22 record high of 9,114.55 as concern mounts that the artificial intelligence boom has peaked. The government said it would temporarily suspend a rule requiring brokerages to maintain collateral worth at least 140 percent of margin loans from Monday through Jan. 31 next year. The move is aimed at preventing forced selling from deepening the market rout. results.title: Korea's shift toward cashless society leaves elderly behind
results.content: A 67-year-old man surnamed Cho living in Bucheon, Gyeonggi Province, recently tried to pay for a cup of coffee at Starbucks with cash, only to be told that the store accepted only credit cards and mobile payments. "I just wanted to pay in cash, but they told me it had been the store's long-standing policy not to accept it. I knew most people paid by card these days, but I never expected a store to refuse cash altogether," he said. "Since then, I've made sure to always carry a card." His experience comes as cash is becoming harder to use in everyday life in Korea, with more cafes, buses and even bank branches moving away from physical payments. For many consumers, paying by card or mobile phone has become the new normal as Korea moves toward a cashless society. results.title: How Disney+'s 'The Remarried Empress' wins over Gen Z, global viewers
results.content: Disney+’s new Korean original series "The Remarried Empress" features Korean actors addressing one another with Western names while navigating a fictional European-style empire in elaborate gowns and military uniforms. When the initial teaser trailers were released, some viewers expressed skepticism, comparing the visual aesthetic to a cosplay convention. However, upon its official premiere on Nov. 3, the series completely shattered expectations. Within just three days of release, the drama officially became the most-watched Disney+ local original series of all time worldwide, based on cumulative global views. Audience feedback across global fan platforms has mirrored this enthusiasm. Viewers who binged the first four episodes highlighted its "slow, subtle, addictive royal drama vibe." results.title: Jinan: Korea's open-air museum of geological wonders
results.content: JINAN, North Jeolla Province — Just a 30-kilometer drive east from Jeonju Station, the rolling green mountains of North Jeolla Province give way to a sight that feels entirely alien yet deeply sacred as two colossal weathered rocks bearing a striking resemblance to a pair of giant horse ears rise abruptly out of the forests of Maisan ("horse ear mountain") Provincial Park. Stepping into this high-plateau region, which forms an integral part of the Jinan-Muju National Geopark, visitors are immersed in the unique landscape that earned Mount Mai three stars in the prestigious Michelin Green Guide, the highest possible rating. First time visitors will immediately be struck by the texture of the mountains. Rather than the granite found in most places on the peninsula, the giant cliffs here are made of conglomerate sedimentary rock, pockmarked with thousands of hollow cavities known as tafoni.

results.content: WASHINGTON — A candidate for the next United Nations secretary-general has emphasized the importance of mediation in addressing international conflicts while responding to South Korea's concerns over tensions on the Korean Peninsula. "Of course, mediation is the most important role of a Secretary General," Feridun Sinirlioglu, a Turkish diplomat currently serving as secretary-general of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe, said during a dialogue with U.N. member states in New York on Friday. During the session, South Korea's representative asked how Sinirlioglu would keep longstanding security issues, including those involving the Korean Peninsula, on the U.N. agenda and help prevent tensions from escalating. results.content: Hosaka Yuji, a Japanese-born naturalized Korean and special professor at Korea University's Graduate School of Public Administration, has identified what Japanese women find attractive about Korean men. The growing number of marriages between Korean men and Japanese women, he said, reflects the popularity of Korean men's affectionate expressions and thoughtfulness among Japanese women. Hosaka made the remarks during an appearance on the YouTube channel Woongdal Bookstore on Sunday. He described this as a clear indication that Japanese women have developed a strong preference for Korean men.
